name: gated-publish
description: Publish lifecycle that teaches the release triangle every estate gets wrong: a human approval (NO auto-release — no default_option, no hold_timeout: a publish that self-releases on a timer is the anti-pattern), an answer-as-data normalizer, and a boolean branch pair. LAW ONE — never branch on a human's raw words: the gate grammar compares values, not intent, so a `when` on out.approve.answer is a string-equality bet on free text; the parse node reads the answer as DATA and emits the boolean, the complementary gate pair (negated when, on_skip prune) routes one arm. LAW TWO — refuse-on-empty-authorization: an answer of bare 'publish' (or anything without an authorization clause) normalizes to authorized=false and the hold arm reports it; the publish node executes ONLY the copy the human's text clearly authorizes, and re-verifies the hash. LAW THREE — machine wait and human question never share a gate: precheck (until_argv, zero tokens) and approve (question, no wait) are separate nodes — the hybrid gate is the ambiguity both estates' validators under-enforce (sys-4zsj9o) and this file never models it. Seeds (run_context map, ALL required): 'artifact_src' = absolute path of the file to publish; 'publish_target' = absolute path the publish node alone may write; 'review_brief' = what the human is asked to approve, verbatim into the gate context. Scratch root /tmp/gated-publish-example holds the staging copy + sha256 sidecar; stage wipes it, so a stale artifact can never ride an old pre-check. every_s/timeout_s are policy, not work: raise them for real cadence without touching any node fingerprint. Receipts walk three paths: authorized publish (executed + hash-verified), bare-'publish' refusal (routed to hold, zero writes), explicit hold with reason.

nodes.goal: Stage the artifact for human approval. 1) rm -rf /tmp/gated-publish-example && mkdir -p /tmp/gated-publish-example (a stale staging file must never ride into a new approval). 2) Copy {run.artifact_src} to /tmp/gated-publish-example/staged.bin — if the source does not exist, do NOT create a stand-in: reply {"staged": false, "why": "source missing"}. 3) Write the line 'sha256sum output' style sidecar: run sha256sum so /tmp/gated-publish-example/staged.bin.sha256 contains '<hex>  staged.bin'. 4) Re-hash the staged copy and compare to the source hash. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"staged": true, "sha256": "<hex>", "size_bytes": <int>, "match": true} — match only if source and staged hashes are equal.

until_argv:
import pathlib,subprocess,sys; S=pathlib.Path('/tmp/gated-publish-example'); B=S/'staged.bin'; M=S/'staged.bin.sha256'
if not (B.exists() and M.exists()): sys.exit(1)
rc=subprocess.run(['sha256sum','-c','staged.bin.sha256'],cwd=str(S),capture_output=True).returncode
S.joinpath('precheck_last.json').write_text('{"sidecar_check_exit": %d}' % rc)
sys.exit(0 if rc==0 else 1)

nodes.question: Stage verified by machine pre-check (sidecar hash confirmed). Publish to {run.publish_target}? Release law: 'publish: <one clause naming exactly what you authorize>' — anything else (bare 'publish', 'yes', vague praise) executes NOTHING and routes to the hold report; 'hold: <why>' routes to the hold report too.

nodes.goal: The human answered the approve gate; its committed answer is in ## Inputs. Read it as DATA — you are a normalizer, not an approver: you approve nothing and write nothing. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"authorized": <true|false>, "scope": "<the authorization clause verbatim if authorized, else ''>", "held_reason": "<the human's text if this is a hold or a refusal, else ''>"}. Rules: authorized=true ONLY when the answer begins with 'publish' (case-insensitive) AND carries a non-empty clause after it clearly naming what is authorized; bare 'publish', 'publish:' with nothing after, or any vague yes is authorized=false with held_reason naming the missing piece.

Execute the authorized publish. The normalized human decision is in ## Inputs (parse payload: authorized + scope; approve answer). SAFETY: copy /tmp/gated-publish-example/staged.bin to {run.publish_target} — that ONE location, nothing else, nothing extra. If the scope text does not clearly cover this copy operation, write NOTHING and reply {"published": false, "refused": "<why>"}. Otherwise copy, re-hash the copy against the stage sha256 (from the stage payload in your Inputs), and reply ONLY fenced json {"published": true, "sha256": "<hex>", "authorized_scope": "<scope verbatim>", "verified": <true iff hashes equal>}.

The publish was NOT authorized (explicit hold, or a bare/vague 'publish' that carried no authorization clause — the parse payload in ## Inputs carries held_reason). Touch no file. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"published": false, "held_because": "<held_reason verbatim>", "next_step": "<one line: the exact release text this would need to execute>"}

Close the publish run: exactly one arm ran (the pruned arm counts as satisfied and injects nothing — say which ran from the payloads in ## Inputs). The pre-check answer (## Inputs from 'precheck') carries attempt + waited_s — report them. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"lane": "publish|hold", "published": <bool from executing arm>, "sha256": "<hex or null>", "precheck_attempts": <int>, "held_because": "<reason or null>"}
